title: .NET 10 RC 2: System.ExecutionEngineException: Illegal instruction: Attempted to execute an instruction code not defined by the processor.
body: My macOS osx-x64 introspection app fails under the .NET 10 RC build with `System.ExecutionEngineException: Illegal instruction: Attempted to execute an instruction code not defined by the processor.` I provided a downloadable app bundle and source-build instructions from the dotnet/macios repository. The fatal output repeats calls to `System.Runtime.EH.GetClasslibException` and `RhThrowHwEx` 135 times before a reflection/custom-attribute stack. I expect the app to execute successfully.

symptoms_visible: My macOS x64 introspection app terminates with `System.ExecutionEngineException: Illegal instruction: Attempted to execute an instruction code not defined by the processor.`
My fatal output repeats `System.Runtime.EH.GetClasslibException` and `RhThrowHwEx` 135 times before the reflection and custom-attribute stack.
N0.label: N0 illegal-instruction crash reported

symptoms_visible: The app still terminates with the illegal-instruction fatal error when I run it under LLDB.
N1.label: N1 debugger evidence collected

symptoms_visible: After one later dependency bump in macios, the introspection app runs successfully for me.
N2_x.label: N2_x transient success after dependency bump

symptoms_visible: A later RC2 integration again terminates with the same illegal-instruction exception.
We also see the illegal-instruction failure in affected perf and EF Core CI workloads.
N3_x.label: N3_x recurring crash after later RC2 integration

symptoms_visible: The illegal-instruction crash remains reproducible in affected artifacts, while the artifact built with the older toolchain runs successfully.
N4.label: N4 build-toolchain matrix collected

symptoms_visible: Fresh builds using the runtime fixes that reached macios run successfully for us.
The previously downloaded self-contained app still crashes because it contains the older broken runtime.
N_terminal.label: terminal fresh fixed build runs successfully

question_patterns: Can you run the app under LLDB and share the backtrace and exception context at the failure?
Can you capture the debugger output around the failure, including the exception code and fault kind?
clarifications.user_answer_in_this_oncall: Under LLDB the process stops with SIGABRT. The backtrace goes through `PROCAbort` and `EEPolicy::HandleFatalError`. Printing `*pExInfo` gives `m_ExceptionCode = 3221225501` and `m_kind = HardwareFault | InstructionFaultFlag`; I pasted the full backtrace and ExInfo output.

counterfactual_candidates.answer: LLDB shows an ordinary managed exception with no hardware or instruction fault, and the process does not enter the runtime fatal-error path.
The same SIGABRT and hardware-instruction-fault context appears at different absolute addresses because address-space layout differs between runs.

edges.comment: From c2-c10. The reporter asked how to capture the requested data; participant1 then debugged the same macios reproduction and supplied the raw LLDB backtrace and ExInfo. That technical reproducer is folded into the simulated user side. The later interpretation of the fault as a malformed write-barrier path remains engineer-side.

solution.intent: Take the next routine macios runtime dependency bump and treat the successful run after that bump as resolving the crash.
solution.concrete_example: Update macios to the next runtime dependency bump, rebuild the introspection app, and rerun it; that particular integration executes successfully.

edges.comment: From reporter c19 and participant4 c21. The reporter independently consumed a normal macios dependency bump and observed a successful run, creating persistent state S2. Participant4 did not accept that as a durable fix and suspected sensitivity to code layout. Later RC2 integrations reproduced the crash, falsifying the bump itself as the solution.

solution.intent: Continue consuming later RC2 integrations on the assumption that the unexplained successful bump means the runtime issue has gone away.
solution.concrete_example: Move to the later RC2 integration and rerun without changing the runtime implementation; the same illegal-instruction crash returns.

edges.comment: From reporter c35 and affected operators c36-c37. A later RC2 integration was persistently consumed as state S3, but the reporter's introspection test failed again. Perf and EF Core operators independently reported the same fatal symptom; those corroborating affected users are folded into the simulated user side rather than treated as separate causal problems.

question_patterns: Can you compare the build-environment metadata for the affected artifacts and the one that worked?
Which toolchain and runner-image versions were recorded for each artifact?
clarifications.user_answer_in_this_oncall: I checked the build metadata. One affected RC build used Xcode 16.4, and the original affected build used Xcode 16.0. The build that worked for us used Xcode 15.4 on the older macOS image. I attached the metadata screenshots for all three.

counterfactual_candidates.answer: Both the failing and working artifacts were produced by the same toolchain version and identical runner image, while only the runtime source revision changed.
The affected builds used two other Xcode 16 point releases, while the working build still used Xcode 15.4.

edges.comment: From c24-c32. Participant5 raised the build-toolchain question, participant1 inspected official build metadata, and the reporter identified the macios integration that worked. These technical contributors are folded into one user side. The screenshots carry only the raw build metadata; concluding that Mach-O subsection handling moved or removed an assembly exit label is engineer-side.

solution.intent: Fix the x64 write-barrier assembly label typing so the Mach-O linker preserves the write-barrier exit containing `rep ret`, rebuild the runtime and self-contained app, and verify the fresh artifact instead of retesting the stale embedded runtime.
solution.concrete_example: Mark the `Exit_WriteWatch_PreGrow64` assembly exit as an alternate/patch label so the Mach-O linker cannot treat it as an independent removable or movable subsection. Rebuild the runtime and then rebuild the self-contained introspection app. Ask the reporter to run that fresh artifact and confirm that it executes successfully; the old downloaded app will continue to carry its broken embedded runtime.
solution.inference_hint: Participant4's disassembly established that `JIT_WriteBarrier_WriteWatch_PreGrow64` branched to an address with no valid exit code immediately before its end marker, even though the source contained a `REPRET` expansion. Participant5 connected this to Mach-O subsection semantics: an untyped, non-local, non-`.alt_entry` exit label could be moved or eliminated by the newer linker. The Xcode build matrix and transient success are raw user-side evidence; identifying linker-sensitive write-barrier layout and correcting the label type are engineer conclusions.

edges.comment: Resolution from c16-c32 and c47-c52. Participant4 diagnosed the malformed write-barrier layout; participant5 proposed correcting the assembly label type; the eventual runtime fix was reported as landed. Reporter c48 confirmed that fresh builds worked once the fixes reached macios. Reporter c50 clarified that the originally downloadable self-contained app embeds the broken runtime and therefore remains invalid as verification of a newer runtime.

satisfaction_conditions: Must identify the accepted root cause: the macOS x64 runtime's `JIT_WriteBarrier_WriteWatch_PreGrow64` could branch past its valid code because Mach-O linker subsection handling moved or removed an improperly typed exit label containing the `rep ret`; this was not an unsupported processor ISA instruction generated for the target CPU.

The diagnosis must be grounded in the collected debugger evidence and build-toolchain matrix, including the hardware-instruction-fault context, the unreachable write-barrier address derived by engineers, and the difference between affected newer-toolchain artifacts and the working older-toolchain artifact.
The fix must correct the write-barrier assembly exit-label typing so the linker preserves the exit code, then rebuild the runtime and any self-contained application that embeds it.

Must not declare the issue fixed merely because one dependency bump happened to run successfully or recommend continuing to consume later RC2 integrations without the targeted runtime fix; the crash returned in a later integration and other workloads.
Must not use the old downloadable self-contained app to judge a newly installed SDK, because that app retains its embedded broken runtime.
Must ask the reporter to verify a fresh application build containing the runtime fix and treat the issue as resolved only after the reporter confirms that fresh builds execute successfully.

persona_hint.experience_level: Experienced .NET and macOS build engineer who can build dotnet/macios from source, consume dependency bumps, run LLDB commands, compare official-build metadata, and distinguish an installed SDK from the runtime embedded in a self-contained application.
persona_hint.communication_style: Concise and highly technical; supplies exact commands, build links, stack traces, and integration revisions; quickly corrects misleading reproduction claims and reports regressions when they return.
